description: The >>EVALUATE / >>WHEN / >>WHEN OTHER / >>END-EVALUATE conditional-compilation directive (ISO §2023:7.3.13, both formats: a selection subject and the TRUE form) - one of the three §2023:7.3.5 conditional-compilation directives. The three words are ONE construct (a >>WHEN outside a >>EVALUATE is not a directive), so they share a row. Implemented by ConditionalCompilationProcessor; the introduction gate rejects the directive words below 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.10: 'The EVALUATE directive provides for multi-branch conditional compilation'; §2002:7.2.4: 'The compiler directives that are used for conditional compilation are the DEFINE directive, the EVALUATE directive, and the IF directive'; and §2002:F.2 names it, its item 32: 'Directives are provided to enable specific lines of source to be included or omitted'. 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.10: 'The EVALUATE directive provides for multi-branch conditional compilation') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.13.1).

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.13.2 general format: a selection subject or TRUE, with >>WHEN objects — evaluated and diagnosed by the conditional-compilation driver as COBOL1619; >>END-EVALUATE writes no operand (checked centrally, §2023:7.3.3 SR3/SR4, as COBOL1911) and the driver's frame stack diagnoses the directive's structure as COBOL2649.

source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725EV.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
       >>EVALUATE TRUE
       >>WHEN 1 = 1
           DISPLAY "X".
       >>END-EVALUATE
           STOP RUN.
